posts.author: Whoosh10
posts.content:
Evap line would just have gas fumes, no leaks. In my experience, a disconnected Evap line smells worse on hot days. 







In all likelihood, your fuel return line needs to be addressed. The soft hose is likely toast and/or the clamping situation is not the best. Is your setup OEM? You might be able to order parts from the dealer (ideal).

posts.author: Bruder
posts.content:
It's definitely a hydraulic line with that grey pipe and hex nut.  Did someone run a aftermarket flexible hose for the clutch and leave this hanging unused? There is a union for 2 pipes near this location on the frame wall.  If you want to diagnose your fuel leak, you can power up the fuel pump without starting the engine by jumping Fp and +B in the diagnostic block behind the fuse box behind the battery. The ignition key needs to be in the on position, but not running, or cranking. Have a fire extinguisher nearby just in case. It only takes a few moments for the system to pressure up.  Use your fingers to touch places like where the fuel damper connects to the rail, and other joints and smell for gas.  A mistake often made is to reuse the copper washers that seal these connections. They are only soft once and reusing them makes them harder resulting in an increased chance for leakage.  I can provide a list of part numbers if you want to replace all of these. The dealer still has them.  Torque connections to spec. You can check for codes using the method found in the 
online manual
.

posts.author: 3p141592654
posts.content:
When I last did my injectors I got some dirt down the holes and that made me super nervous.  I think its almost impossible to avoid unless your engine is squeaky clean.  Mine had lots of oily gunk all over the head and manifold. So I hooked up a some small diameter tygon tubing to the shop vac and I actually vacuumed out the crap through the hole.  I used a borescope to check it was clean. So you might as well start picking at it and once its removed vacuum out the junk that fell in. To be super anal you could put that cylinder on TDC so that the valves are closed. 







Based on the picture it almost looks like some sort of sealant was added to those seals.  That may explain the degraded rubber and difficulty removing them.  Old seals are usually very hard but come out in one piece in my experience.
